claims: An Ayatollah is a high-ranking title for Twelver Shia clergy specializing in Islamic studies, jurisprudence, and theology.
The Ayatollah title is commonly used in Iran.
Ruhollah Khomeini served as Supreme Leader of Iran.
Ali Khamenei served as Supreme Leader of Iran.
Ali Khamenei served as Iran’s Supreme Leader from 1989 until his death on February 28, 2026.
Mojtaba Khamenei is the son of Ali Khamenei.
The Ayatollah title is typically given to Shia scholars when their teachers and peers recognize their expertise in seminaries, often in Qom.
The Assembly of Experts selects the Supreme Leader.
The term Ayatollah literally translates to "Sign of God" or "Sign of Allah".
